# Performance circuits {#sec-performance}

Two wide circuits are provided to test the performance. They are found in
`resources/examples/performance.py`. They are used to check that many Bloch spheres can
be drawn at the same time, and that a long JSON file is handled without a
problem.

## `ghz(count)` {.unnumbered}

A GHZ state is prepared on `count` qubits. The circuit is shallow: one Hadamard
gate, and a chain of CNOT gates. Every qubit is fully entangled with the others,
so every Bloch vector has length zero. This is a good first test for the number
of spheres, because the state is easy to verify.

## `layered(count, depth=4, seed=1234)` {.unnumbered}

A random layered circuit is built. Each layer is a rotation on every qubit,
followed by a brickwork of CZ gates. The rotations give non-trivial Bloch
vectors, and the depth controls the number of native steps. A seed is used, so
the circuit is reproducible.

## Generating the files {.unnumbered}

```bash
make outputs
```

The script compiles a small set of circuits and writes the JSON files to `out/`.
It also writes `out/manifest.json`, which lists every file with a readable
label. The viewer reads that manifest, so a new file appears in the selector as
soon as it is generated.

| File | Qubits | Native steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bell.json` | 2 | 7 |
| `ghz3.json` | 3 | 12 |
| `ghz16.json` | 16 | 77 |
| `layered16.json` | 16 | 676 |
| `adder_n2_1_1.json` | 4 | 187 |

The numbers are given for the built-in simulator. The 16-qubit circuits are the
performance tests. The `layered16` circuit is the heaviest one: it has 16
spheres and 676 steps.

## Opening the files {.unnumbered}

```bash
make outputs
python -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000/frontend/index.html
```

The file `source/frontend/index.html` is connected to the generated files. It loads
`out/manifest.json`, fills the selector with the available files, and opens the
default one. The other files can be chosen in the selector. The number of qubits
and the number of steps are shown, together with a live frame-rate counter, so
that the performance can be watched while the view is rotated.
